images.filename: Saratoga Springs Public Library north end.jpg
images.caption: The Saratoga Springs Public Library, located at 49 Henry Street in Saratoga Springs, New York, was built in 1993-1995 and was designed by Architecture Plus of Troy, New York and The LA Group and Phillips Associates of Saratoga Springs. (Source: [1])  The library's original location, built in 1950, was at 320 Broadway at the corner of Spring Street in Congress Park, now the headquarters of Saratoga Arts.  The founding of a public library was approved by the voters in 1945.  Prior to that, the city's only library was the Saratoga Athenaeum, a private subscription library founded in 1885.

images.filename: Congress Park Columbian Fountain, Saratoga Spring.jpg
images.caption: The Columbian Fountain in Congress Park, Saratoga Springs, New York features the waters of George Putnam's Columbian Spring (1806). The domed pavilion is a modern reproduction of the original early-19th century Greek structure. (Source: [1])

images.caption: The Adelphia Hotel located at 361–365 Broadway in Saratoga Springs, New York, was built in 1877 and is the last surviving hotel in the city from the 19th century. The porch, which features slender columns and open spandrels became known as the "Saratoga porch" because it was typical of the time and place. The hotel is part of the Broadway Historic District, which was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.
